assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt the base_frame to the floor plane with the left_upright, right_upright, rear_spine, lower_cross_rail, and upper_cross_rail to form an open inspection rack. 2. Mount input_plate on the front of the base frame, then set embedding_table directly above it and connect both to the residual_bus. 3. Install the residual_bus vertically through the centre and fasten layer_tray_001 through layer_tray_128_marker to it in order, leaving the exploded_block_064 tray pulled forward for inspection. 4. On the port/left lane of exploded_block_064, install attn_pre_norm, q_projection_bank, mla_down_projection, kv_latent_cache_a, kv_latent_cache_b, kv_up_projection, qk_rope_norm, flash_attention_core, and o_projection, then connect o_projection back to residual_bus. 5. On the starboard/right lane, install ffn_pre_norm, router_gate, group_limit_selector, expert_alltoall_bus, routed_expert_tile_a through routed_expert_tile_d, shared_expert, overflow_shared_expert, fp4_qat_plate, and moe_combine_gate, then connect moe_combine_gate back to residual_bus. 6. Install final_norm and prediction_head above the last tray, then attach mtp_block_1, mtp_block_2, primary_lm_loss, and mtp_loss_node to the output side. 7. Mount kv_memory_scale beside the cache pages, muon_optimizer and adamw_carveout on the service shelf, and parallelism_panel plus training_data_pipe on the rear right side. 8. Verify that every functional module has a visible parent connection, no part penetrates the ground plane, and the exposed exploded tray can be read from the ISO, front, side, and top views.

info.summary: PROJECTED next-generation flagship from Zhipu / Z.ai, extrapolated from GLM-4.5's published research direction. No public paper at scene time. Best guess: ~600B total / ~48B activated, deep-narrow at 128 × 5760, GQA(96/8) augmented with an MLA-style compressed KV down-projection, 1 shared + 256 routed experts (top-8) with group-limited dispatch, depth-2 MTP for stronger speculative decoding, Muon optimiser adopted for the matrix bulk, FP4 QAT on routed experts, and 256K native context. Treat numbers as plausible extrapolation, not fact.
info.description:
GLM-5.1 is presented here as a research-trajectory PROJECTION, not a paper. Where GLM-4.5 went deep-narrow with 96 layers / 5120 hidden / 160 experts top-8 + 1 shared + group-limited routing, GLM-5.1 likely (i) adds another ~33% depth (128 layers) and a small width bump (5760), (ii) doubles the routed-expert count (160 → 256) while keeping top-8 active, (iii) adopts an MLA-style learned KV compression on top of GQA — a known cross-pollination trick from DeepSeek-V3 — to halve KV memory at long context, (iv) raises MTP depth from 1 to 2 (small quality + speculative-decoding wins), (v) extends native context from 128K to 256K via training rather than YaRN, (vi) crosses over to the Muon optimiser for the matrix bulk after its DeepSeek-V4 success, while keeping AdamW for the carve-out (embed / head / RMSNorm / mHC scalars / router bias), and (vii) brings FP4 QAT to routed experts.

Design rationale, in one line each:
• Deeper-narrower still: more layers > wider hidden for reasoning at fixed FLOPs.
• 256 fine-grained experts: doubles capacity without changing the active-FLOPs budget.
• MLA on top of GQA: stacks two KV-shrinking tricks for cheap 256K context.
• Depth-2 MTP: ~2.4× speculative speedup vs depth-1.
• Muon adoption: ~5–10% wall-clock saving at this scale per the V4 results.
• FP4 experts: ~4× expert-weight memory shrink vs BF16.

comparisons.delta: Same family. Projected GLM-5.1 grows: total params 355B → 600B, activated 32B → 48B (~50% larger compute / token), depth 96 → 128 (deeper), width 5120 → 5760 (slightly wider), routed experts 160 → 256, KV path GQA → GQA+MLA, MTP depth 1 → 2, optimiser AdamW-only → Muon+AdamW, native ctx 32K (trained) / 128K (YaRN) → 256K (trained). Routing scheme (sigmoid loss-free + group-limited ≤4 of 8) is preserved unchanged because the V4.5 design study showed it scales well.

Different bets. V4-Pro pushes attention sparsity (CSA+HCA hybrid + lightning indexer) and has 384 routed experts top-6. GLM-5.1 stays dense-attention (GQA+MLA) but doubles down on depth and expert count. Activated params per token are similar (~48B vs ~49B), but V4-Pro has ~3× more total capacity and natively supports 1M context vs GLM-5.1's projected 256K. GLM keeps the deep-narrow doctrine; V4 stays moderately wide (7168) and very deep (61).

GLM-5.1 is the most CONSERVATIVE projection — it does not add linear / hybrid attention. Qwen3.6 likely adopts Gated DeltaNet (linear) for 75% of layers; MiniMax-M2.7 likely pushes the lightning:softmax ratio further. GLM stays with full softmax + MLA-compressed KV, betting that depth + expert count + a small KV trick beats hybrid attention at the 256K context point.

Public consensus on GPT-5-class peers is unstable. Versus the most-rumoured shape (large dense or coarse-MoE with full softmax + GQA + FP8), GLM-5.1 is much sparser per token (48B activated of 600B), uses an extra MLA layer on top of GQA (smaller KV), and is open-weight. Activated FLOPs / token in projected GLM-5.1 are far below a comparably-capable closed dense model — the cost story is the entire pitch.

parts.name: Open Base Frame
parts.role: Grounded rack base that roots the full projected GLM-5.1 assembly and keeps every subsystem visible.

parts.name: Port Upright Rail
parts.role: Left structural post that carries the attention and cache inspection lane.

parts.name: Starboard Upright Rail
parts.role: Right structural post that carries the MoE, parallelism, and optimiser service lane.

parts.name: Rear Residual Spine Support
parts.role: Rear post aligning all visible layer trays to the central residual bus.

parts.name: Lower Cross Rail
parts.role: Lower transverse rail that locates the input, embedding, and first layer trays.

parts.name: Upper Cross Rail
parts.role: Upper transverse rail that fixes the prediction and MTP head modules above the 128-layer stack.

parts.name: Input Tokens
parts.role: Token-ID stream from the projected multilingual tokenizer enters the rack at floor level.

parts.name: Embedding Table V≈152K by d=5760
parts.role: Tied embedding matrix converts token IDs to the 5760-wide residual stream and is trained by AdamW.

parts.name: Residual Bus d=5760
parts.role: Central residual stream carrying hidden states through the projected 128 pre-norm transformer layers.

parts.name: Layer Tray 1
parts.role: First visible transformer tray; it establishes the repeated attention-plus-MoE layer pitch.

parts.name: Layer Tray 16
parts.role: Representative early-depth transformer tray compressed from layers 2 through 16.

parts.name: Layer Tray 32
parts.role: Visible tray marking the first quarter of the projected 128-layer depth.

parts.name: Layer 64 Exploded Tray
parts.role: Mid-stack transformer block pulled forward as an exploded cutaway so attention and MoE internals remain visible.

parts.name: Layer Tray 80
parts.role: Visible tray marking the post-exploded depth section of the deep-narrow stack.

parts.name: Layer Tray 96
parts.role: Visible tray corresponding to the full depth of GLM-4.5 before the projected GLM-5.1 extension.

parts.name: Layer Tray 112
parts.role: Visible tray in the projected extra-depth segment beyond GLM-4.5.

parts.name: Layer Tray 128 Final
parts.role: Final transformer tray completing the projected 128-layer residual tower.

parts.name: Attention Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: Pre-normalises the residual stream before the attention projections in the exploded layer.

parts.name: 96-Head Q Projection Bank
parts.role: Projects d=5760 hidden states into 96 query heads for dense causal attention.
parts.flops_per_token: ≈2·d·d for the query-side projection at model width

parts.name: MLA KV Down-Projection c_kv≈768
parts.role: Compresses K and V into a learned 768-dimensional latent so long-context cache storage is reduced.
parts.memory_footprint: Stores c_kv≈768 latent bytes per token per layer before reconstruction

parts.name: KV Latent Cache Page A
parts.role: First visible cache page stores MLA latent keys and values for the 256K native context window.
parts.memory_footprint: ≈25 GiB per 256K-token sequence across 128 layers at FP8 latent scale

parts.name: KV Latent Cache Page B
parts.role: Second visible cache page shows the paged long-context memory path rather than hiding it in one cylinder.
parts.memory_footprint: FP8 latent cache is projected at roughly half plain GQA(8) storage

parts.name: KV Up-Projection Reconstructor
parts.role: Reconstructs full K and V tensors from the cached MLA latent before attention scoring.

parts.name: QK-Norm and Partial RoPE
parts.role: Applies QK RMSNorm and partial rotary position encoding before the attention kernel.

parts.name: FlashAttention-3 Causal Core
parts.role: Computes dense causal attention over the projected 256K context using tiled GPU kernels.

parts.name: Attention O Projection
parts.role: Projects attention output back to d=5760 and adds it to the residual bus.

parts.name: 256K Context Scale Gauge
parts.role: Vertical gauge annotates that the cache lane is sized for the projected 256K native context.

parts.name: MoE FFN Pre-RMSNorm
parts.role: Pre-normalises the residual stream before the routed SwiGLU expert layer.

parts.name: Top-8 Sigmoid Router
parts.role: Scores 256 routed experts and selects the top 8 with loss-free balance bias.

parts.name: ≤4 of 8 Group Limiter
parts.role: Constrains selected experts to at most four of eight device groups to bound all-to-all traffic.

parts.name: Expert All-to-All Bus
parts.role: Dispatches token slices to expert-parallel shards and combines the returned activations.

parts.name: Routed Expert Tile A 1-64
parts.role: Visible quarter of the 256 fine-grained SwiGLU expert bank, representing experts 1 through 64.
parts.memory_footprint: 64 experts × 3·5760·1408 FP4 weights in this visible quarter

parts.name: Routed Expert Tile B 65-128
parts.role: Visible quarter of the routed expert bank, representing experts 65 through 128.

parts.name: Routed Expert Tile C 129-192
parts.role: Visible quarter of the routed expert bank, representing experts 129 through 192.

parts.name: Routed Expert Tile D 193-256
parts.role: Visible quarter of the routed expert bank, representing experts 193 through 256.
parts.flops_per_token: Top-8 active experts cost ≈400 MFLOP per layer at d_ff≈1408

parts.name: Always-On Shared Expert
parts.role: Single shared expert handles common computation for every token alongside the top-8 routed experts.

parts.name: Capacity Overflow Shared Expert
parts.role: Projected overflow path absorbs tokens when routed expert capacity is saturated.

parts.name: FP4 QAT Expert Weight Plate
parts.role: Quantisation-aware FP4 plate marks the projected fourfold routed-expert weight memory reduction versus BF16.
parts.memory_footprint: Routed FFN weights projected at roughly 0.25× BF16 storage

parts.name: Weighted MoE Combine Gate
parts.role: Reweights and sums the eight routed expert outputs plus shared-expert output before the residual add.

parts.name: Final RMSNorm
parts.role: Normalises the final residual state before tied vocabulary projection and MTP heads.

parts.name: Tied LM Head
parts.role: Projects final hidden states back to the approximately 152K-token vocabulary using tied embedding weights.

parts.name: MTP Block t+1
parts.role: First multi-token prediction block predicts the t+1 token for speculative decoding.

parts.name: MTP Block t+2
parts.role: Second multi-token prediction block extends the projected MTP depth to 2 for faster speculative decoding.
parts.algorithm: for k in 1..2: h_k=mtp_block_k(h_final); logits_k=h_k@E.T; loss+=w_k*CE(logits_k,target_t+k)

parts.name: Primary LM Loss
parts.role: Primary next-token cross-entropy objective for the tied language-model head.

parts.name: Depth-2 MTP Loss
parts.role: Auxiliary weighted loss trains t+1 and t+2 prediction heads jointly with the main objective.

parts.name: Muon Matrix Optimizer
parts.role: Projected Muon optimizer service module applies Newton-Schulz orthonormalised updates to matrix parameters.
parts.memory_footprint: Uses one momentum buffer rather than AdamW's two moment buffers for matrix bulk

parts.name: AdamW Carve-Out Optimizer
parts.role: Keeps AdamW for embeddings, LM head, RMSNorm weights, router bias, attention sinks, and scalar carve-outs.

parts.name: TP EP PP DP Parallelism Panel
parts.role: Shows the tensor, expert, pipeline, and data parallel axes that make the projected MoE trainable.

parts.name: Training Data Pipe ~30T Tokens
parts.role: Floor-level intake pipe represents the projected roughly 30-trillion-token pretraining and reasoning-RL data stream.
